one_month_reasoning: Scheduled company events in the 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-31 window are thin. Q2 results came out on 28 July, so Q3 results would normally land around late October or early November. I treat them as possibly, but probably not, inside the window. Q3 should look better than Q2: the ~10,000 dmt of Peru concentrate stuck by port closures was shipped in early July, and the BC cost overrun is guided to ease. Against that, gold has fallen from a Q2 realized ~$4,508/oz to ~$4,187 and LME copper is ~$14,335/t, about 3% below its early-September record. The Copper World sanction decision is guided for 'late 2026'. It could come with the DFS and a higher capex figure, which is a two-sided event and more likely Nov-Dec. The stock sits 19% below its 52-week high after a sharp September pullback with copper. With no strong dated catalyst, I keep a near-symmetric lognormal centred just under spot ($26.10). I use monthly vol of ~16.5%, a bit below the 18% that 63%/3.5 gives, because the realized figure is inflated by the one-year rally.

fair_value.method: Blend of SOTP/EV-EBITDA ($25.1, 50%), P/E ($23.3, 25%) and FCF yield ($24.8, 25%). It is built on 2027E attributable EBITDA of ~$1.25B, adj EPS ~$1.55 and FCF ~$550M, which is spot copper/gold with a ~10% mean-reversion haircut, and 444M shares.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Operating assets: 2027E adj EBITDA $1.25B x 7.0x = $8.75B; Copper World 70% stake $1.4B; Cactus $1.0B; net debt ex-Copper-World restricted cash ~$0B by end-2027; 444M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: TTM $1.27B was earned at LME Cu ~$5.9-6.1/lb and Au ~$4,300-4,500. Spot is Cu $6.50 and Au $4,187. I haircut realized prices ~10% for the surplus and record-inventory evidence in [12],[13] and for BC/fuel cost pressure in [1]. Volumes are flat at the guidance midpoint.
A mid-cycle multiple for a BB-/Ba3 mid-tier copper-gold producer. I discount it because these are peak-cycle earnings; HBM's current EV of ~$11.6B is ~9x TTM EBITDA.
Mitsubishi pays $420M + $180M = $600M for 30%, which implies $2.0B for 100%. 70% of that is $1.4B. No premium is added because DFS capex is guided higher than the 2023 PFS.
Paid with 46.8M shares (~$1.5B per [3]). I haircut it by a third for the acquisition premium and for its pre-PFS-update stage.
Reported net debt of -$80.5M includes $334.5M of cash restricted to Copper World, so ex-CW net debt is ~$254M. H2-26 and 2027 FCF after growth capex (~$115M/yr in BC) roughly retires it.

H1-26 annualizes to $1.38 and Q2 sales were depressed by the port delay, which gives a ~$1.70 run-rate at spot. I take ~10% off for metal-price mean reversion and the share count rising to 444M after the ASCU issuance.
Downgrades to hold/sector perform ([3],[17]) argue against a premium multiple on earnings at cyclically high metal prices. 15x is the middle of the historical diversified-miner range.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2027E FCF $550M / 444M shares = $1.24/sh at a 5% required yield

inputs_detail.derivation: H1-26 FCF of $205M annualizes to ~$410M, with sales held back in Q2. Adding the deferred concentrate and spot prices gives ~$600M. I trim it for BC New Ingerbelle growth capex staying ~$115M in 2027 and the Cactus spend.
BB-/Ba3 credit with 6.125% 2029 notes. An equity FCF yield of ~5% is roughly the note coupon less modest growth, reflecting copper growth optionality.

bear.story: Copper falls back toward $4.75-5.00/lb as the refined surplus and the highest exchange inventories since 2003 bite and US tariff-driven COMEX stockpiles unwind. Gold keeps sliding from $4,500 to ~$3,500. The Copper World DFS shows a large capex increase at sanction, and Hudbay's 70% share is funded from 2028. BC costs stay above guidance, and a Peru political or community disruption hits Constancia. EBITDA falls to ~$0.8B and the stock rerates to 6x.

base.story: Metals hold near current levels with some giveback. Guidance is delivered, Copper World is sanctioned with a moderate capex increase, and the balance sheet stays near net-neutral. Earnings at peak prices cap the multiple, so the stock roughly tracks fair value ($24.6) to analyst targets ($35).

bull.story: Copper pushes past $7/lb on supply disruptions and electrification demand while gold holds above $4,000. Copper World is sanctioned with robust economics and Cactus is folded into a staged Arizona hub. The stock rerates toward or above the top of the analyst range ($43).

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$16, about 39% under spot and below the bottom of the 52-week range's recovery leg, the price implies roughly $0.8B normalized EBITDA. That level would most likely mean a fundamental break rather than noise: a copper price collapse below ~$5/lb, a Copper World capex blowout or funding strain that forces equity issuance, or a material Constancia (Peru) disruption.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results (Q2 was released 28 July); Peru shipments catch-up, BC cost recovery, gold price drop
Copper World DFS and sanction decision; DFS guided to show higher capex than 2023 PFS
2027 production, cost and capex guidance plus Q4 2026 results; Copper World capital split with Mitsubishi
Mitsubishi second $180M contribution due within 18 months of the Jan 2026 close
LSIB/USIB challenges to New Ingerbelle permits (judicial review) in BC

key_uncertainties: Copper price path: it is at record levels (~$14,300/t) while combined exchange inventories hit their highest since 2003 in May 2026
Gold price, which supplies 38% of revenue: already down from ~$4,500 to ~$4,190
Copper World DFS capex size and how Hudbay funds its 70% share from 2028
Value and integration of the all-stock Cactus/ASCU acquisition (46.8M shares, ~11% dilution)
Peru political and community risk at Constancia; BC cost overruns and New Ingerbelle permit challenges
Management transition (COO retiring end-Sept 2026) and insider selling earlier in 2026
reasoning: Basic facts come from the Q2-26 MD&A [1]. Hudbay is in good shape: TTM EBITDA is a record $1.27B, ex-CW net debt is ~$254M (headline -$80.5M includes $334.5M restricted to Copper World), credit was upgraded to BB-/Ba3 [9,10], and costs are guided lower. As the skeptic I looked for what consensus (avg target ~$35, Strong Buy [15]) could be getting wrong. (1) Earnings sit on peak metal prices. Copper is ~$6.50/lb versus a $4.36 Q2-25 LME average [1,14], and bears point to a refined surplus with exchange inventories at a 23-year high [12,13]. Gold, 38% of revenue, is already falling: Q2 realized $4,508 versus ~$4,187 now [14,18]. The 11 September 7% drop on a copper pullback shows the beta [5]. (2) Capital intensity is rising. The Copper World DFS will show higher capex than the PFS [1,16], with Hudbay's 70% share funded from 2028. The all-stock Cactus deal diluted ~11% and drew a downgrade [3]. NBF moved to Sector Perform in January [17]. BC costs ran at $3.22/lb against $1.50-2.50 guidance, and growth capex there went up $30M [1]. (3) Permitting and litigation remain live on two growth assets: First Nations challenges at New Ingerbelle [6] and right-of-way and air-permit suits at Copper World [7,8]. (4) Insiders filed to sell in March 2026, including ~220k shares by the departing COO [11]. That is weak evidence on its own. Weighed honestly, none of this is a broken thesis: the balance sheet is strong, Mitsubishi is funding the next CW phase, and FCF is real ($205M in H1 [1]). My blended fair value of $24.6 sits ~6% below spot. It values the business at ~7x haircut EBITDA plus CW and Cactus at deal-implied values, cross-checked with P/E and FCF yield. The analyst range ($29.5-43) is the bull counterweight. For the distribution I use a lognormal with median ~$25.3 and sigma ~0.50. That sigma is below the 63% realized figure, which the run-up inflated, but above the large-cap base rate given the commodity beta. I added a little left-tail mass for the copper mean-reversion scenario. The implied mean of ~$28 is consistent with the scenario mean of $26.25 plus right skew. Research was limited to about 20 queries and fetches. X/Twitter and the major sell-side reports were not consulted directly.
